~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
              Native Win32/Cygwin Linux4BE Developers HowTo
                            jal0@linux4.be

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1.INITIAL ENVIRONMENT SETTINGS:

!!!! MAKE SURE YOUR HOME DIRECTORY PATH DOES NOT CONTAIN ANY SPACES

#### cygwin1.dll version: 1.3.10
#### gcc version: 2.95.3-5 (cygwin special)
#### uname output: CYGWIN_NT-5.0

bash$ export target=mipsel-linux
bash$ export prefix=~/toolchains/xLinux4BE
bash$ export archive=$prefix/archive
bash$ export MAKE_MODE=UNIX


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
2.GETTING THE SOURCES:

bash$ mkdir -p $archive
bash$ cd $archive

#### Login into CVS tree at http://linux-mips.sourceforge.net/ to get 
#### the linux-mips modifications for the linux kernel. Press "Return" 
#### when prompted for password. You only need to do this once on any 
#### machine.

bash$ cvs -d:pserver:anonymous@cvs.linux-mips.sourceforge.net:/cvsroot/linux-mips login

#### Check out a copy of the tree.

bash$ cvs -z3 -d:pserver:anonymous@cvs.linux-mips.sourceforge.net:/cvsroot/linux-mips co linux

#### Take a look of ./linux/Makefile and determine the kernel version to 
#### download. To avoid name conflict, rename linux directory to 
#### sf-linux-$sf_version, Then pack it up for storage.

bash$ version=$(grep ^VERSION\ *=\ * ./linux/Makefile | sed -e s%VERSION\ *=\ *%%)
bash$ patchlevel=$(grep ^PATCHLEVEL\ *=\ * ./linux/Makefile | sed -e s%PATCHLEVEL\ *=\ *%%)
bash$ sublevel=$(grep ^SUBLEVEL\ *=\ * ./linux/Makefile | sed -e s%SUBLEVEL\ *=\ *%%)
bash$ export sf_version=$version.$patchlevel.$sublevel
bash$ mv linux sf-linux-$sf_version
bash$ cd sf-linux-$sf_version; tar -zcvpf ../sf-linux-$sf_version.tar.gz .; cd ..

#### Goto http://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/ to grab the right
#### version of kernel source.

bash$ wget -P$archive http://www.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/v$version.$patchlevel/linux-$sf_version.tar.gz

#### Get the linux4BE kernel sources
bash$ linux4BE_version=20020706
bash$ wget -P$archive  http://www.linux4.be/download/kernel/linux4be$linux4BE_version.tgz 


#### Goto ftp://ftp.kernel.org and get a copy of binutils

bash$ export binutils_version=2.12.90.0.4
bash$ wget -P$archive ftp://ftp.kernel.org/pub/linux/devel/binutils/binutils-$binutils_version.tar.gz

#### Goto ftp://ftp.gnu.org and get copies of gcc and glibc.

bash$ export gcc_version=3.0.4
bash$ export glibc_version=2.2.4
bash$ wget -P$archive ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gcc/gcc-$gcc_version/gcc-$gcc_version.tar.gz 
bash$ wget -P$archive ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/glibc/glibc-$glibc_version.tar.gz 
bash$ wget -P$archive ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/glibc/glibc-linuxthreads-$glibc_version.tar.gz

#### Get a default kernel ramdisk image to play with.

bash$ wget -P$archive http://www.linux4.be/download/ramdisk/ramdisk.gz


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
3.INSTALLING THE SOURCES:


bash$ mkdir -p $prefix/build
bash$ cd $prefix/build

#### Install the Linux Kernel Sources

bash$ tar -xzf $archive/linux-$sf_version.tar.gz
bash$ cd $prefix/build/linux

#### Install the mipsel-linux kernel Sources

bash$ tar -xzf $archive/sf-linux-$sf_version.tar.gz

#### Install the linux4BE kernel Sources

bash$ tar -xzf $archive/linux4be$linux4BE_version.tgz

#### Install binutils Sources

bash$ cd $prefix/build
bash$ tar -xzf $archive/binutils-$binutils_version.tar.gz

#### Install gcc Sources

bash$ cd $prefix/build
bash$ tar -xzf $archive/gcc-$gcc_version.tar.gz

#### Install libc sources

bash$ cd $prefix/build
bash$ tar -xzf $archive/glibc-$glibc_version.tar.gz
bash$ cd glibc-$glibc_version 
bash$ tar -xzf $archive/glibc-linuxthreads-$glibc_version.tar.gz 


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
4.BUILD CROSS-BINUTILS:


bash$ cd $prefix/build/binutils-$binutils_version
bash$ ./configure --target=$target --prefix=$prefix > ../binutils-configure.log 2>&1
bash$ make > ../binutils-build.log 2>&1
bash$ make install > ../binutils-install.log 2>&1
bash$ cd .. 

#### add to path so cross-binutils can be found

bash$ export PATH=$PATH:$prefix/bin

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
5.BUILD GCC 'C' BOOTSTRAP CROSS-COMPILER:


#### build & install the bootstap compiler

bash$ cd $prefix/build/gcc-$gcc_version
bash$ ./configure --target=$target --prefix=$prefix --without-headers --with-newlib --disable-shared > ../gcc-bootstrap-configure.log 2>&1
bash$ make all-gcc > ../gcc-bootstrap-build.log 2>&1
bash$ make install-gcc > ../gcc-bootstrap-install.log 2>&1


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
6.CONFIGURE THE KERNEL SOURCES:

bash$ cd $prefix/build/linux

#### set up default device configuration file. You may have to add the
#### following in .config to the frambuffer section following 
#### CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE=y:
	CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE_MEMBASE=aa200000
	CONFIG_FB_SIMPLE_MEMSIZE=0

bash$ make CROSS_COMPILE=$target- mrproper
bash$ cp config_be300 .config

#### configure linux for device

bash$ make CROSS_COMPILE=$target- oldconfig
bash$ make CROSS_COMPILE=$target- dep > ../kernel-dep.log 2>&1
bash$ make CROSS_COMPILE=$target- clean


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
7.BUILDING THE GLIBC RUNTIME LIBRARY:

#### create kernel source simlinks

bash$ cd $prefix/mipsel-linux
bash$ mkdir include 
bash$ cd include 
bash$ ln -s $prefix/build/linux/include/asm-mips asm 
bash$ ln -s $prefix/build/linux/include/linux linux

#### configure & install

bash$ cd $prefix/build
bash$ mkdir glibc-build
bash$ cd glibc-build
bash$ CC=$target-gcc $prefix/build/glibc-$glibc_version/configure --host=$target --prefix=$prefix --with-headers=$prefix/$target/include --enable-add-ons --disable-sanity-checks --disable-debug --disable-profile > ../glibc-configure.log 2>&1

#### sitback, this may take a while!

bash$ make > ../glibc-build.log 2>&1

#### change files with .exe extensions so they can be installed

bash$ for i in $(find . -name '*.exe' -printf %p\ ) ; do mv -f $i $(echo $i | sed -e s%.exe%%) ; done 

#### install

bash$ make install_root=$prefix/$target prefix="" install > ../glibc-install.log 2>&1

#### fix library

bash$ echo "GROUP ( libc.so.6 libc_nonshared.a )" > $prefix/$target/lib/libc.so

#### change files with .exe extensions for target platform

bash$ cd $prefix/$target/bin
bash$ for i in $(find . -name '*.exe' -printf %p\ ) ; do mv -f $i $(echo $i | sed -e s%.exe%%) ; done 


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
8.REBUILD GCC 'C/C++' CROSS-COMPILER:

bash$ cd $prefix/build/gcc-$gcc_version
bash$ make clean
bash$ ./configure --target=$target --prefix=$prefix --enable-languages=c,c++ > ../gcc-configure.log 2>&1
bash$ make > ../gcc-build.log 2>&1
bash$ install > ../gcc-install.log 2>&1


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
9.CREATING A RAMDISK

#### copy over the default ramdisk.
^^^^ NOTE: Step 9 & 10 can be done after Step 7. before rebuilding gcc.

bash$ cd $prefix/build/linux
bash$ cp $archive/ramdisk.gz ./arch/mips/ramdisk


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
10.BUILD THE LINUX KERNEL

bash$ cd $prefix/build/linux
bash$ make CROSS_COMPILE=$target- vmlinux > ../kernel-vmlinux.log 2>&1
